title: An F_p-algebra is absolutely weakly normal if and only if it is perfect
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises perfect F_p-algebras as exactly the absolutely weakly normal ones, which means that the two existence conditions on roots, x^3 = y^2 implies x is a square and y a cube, and l^l x = y^l implies a^l = x and l a = y for a prime l, hold in A (statement lines 12124-12128). One direction is immediate from condition (2)(b) of the seminormal-ring definition, but the converse is a case analysis on the prime p that uses perfectness in a genuinely arithmetic way: for p > 3 one writes p = 2n + 3m with n, m > 0, takes a^p = x and b^p = y, and checks c = a^n b^m satisfies c^{2p} = x^p hence c^2 = x and similarly c^3 = y; for p = 2 one writes x = a^2 and deduces a^3 = y from a^6 = y^2; and for p = 3 one writes y = a^3 and deduces x = a^2 from x^3 = a^6 (proof lines 12136-12146). The second condition is then disposed of by splitting on whether the prime l equals p (proof lines 12148-12152). The representation p = 2n + 3m and the reduction of the root-taking to taking p-th roots are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.
